notes: Catalogue says the breadboard top half ('t') is rows a-e and bottom half ('b') is rows f-j, whereas the image labels them j-f (top) and e-a (bottom). I used the catalogue naming. Only strip membership matters.

Column and rail positions were estimated from the image. Rail hole numbers (tn.1, tp.1, tn.12, tn.28, bn.4, bn.10, bp.6, bp.14 and so on) are approximate. Parts that share a column strip were put on different rows.
The Arduino black wire goes to a GND pin in the power header. I assumed GND.1 for it.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap with its four legs in columns 4 and 6. Pin 2 and the 10k pulldown meet at column 4. The 5V rail connects at column 6.
The manual's text says analog input 2, but the circuit, schematic and code all use A0. I used A0.
The LED anode is on the same strip as the 220 ohm resistor. The cathode strip goes to the ground rail by a black wire.
The two 10k resistors are both shown as 10k ohm. I wrote the value as 10000 and the other resistor as 220.
